correctness.rationale: Every perfect matching of the explicit 24-vertex cubic graph is recovered by an exhaustive vertex-covering recursion (60 distinct 12-edge matchings). For each matching, deleting \(S\subseteq E\setminus M\) isolates it exactly when S hits each other perfect matching; all \(\binom{24}{k}\) deletion subsets for k=0 through the first feasible k≤6 are enumerated. This proves both optimum lower/upper bounds and counts all minimal S; outputs yield 40 optima 5, 20 optima 6, refined counts 8/4 for three 8-cycles, 0/6 for two 12-cycles, 32/10 for one 24-cycle. A separate explicit edge-list recursion and exact MILP replicates all 60 optima, with all stored witnesses directly checked. Computations are finite proof steps and executable artifacts are present.

originality.rationale: The claim is an exact anti-forcing distribution and a two-factor-profile separation for the McGee (3,7)-cage, not the prior definitions or universal hitting condition. The earliest relevant anti-forcing theory (Lei–Yeh–Zhang, 2014) gives an exact set-cover characterization for any graph but not the computed McGee spectrum or its refined 2-factor table. Deng–Zhang (2016) and Alikhani–Soltani (2017) have different objects, with no McGee statement in the inspected material. published-finding corpus matching-related records and accessible historical claims concern different invariants; direct searches for this theorem found no covering result. The possibility of an unindexed or inaccessible equivalent result remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent McGee anti-forcing distribution may be indexed under another name or missing from the inspected databases.

The theorem is finite; no uniform claim about all cubic cages follows.

value.rationale: The unique (3,7)-cage is a natural, non-vertex-transitive smallest high-girth cubic graph; matching anti-forcing measures the minimum edge damage required to isolate a perfect matching. Exact distribution over all 60 matchings and 18,200 minimal deletion certificates determines the first complete benchmark for this graph, and the sharp two-factor table supplies a motivated counterexample to the idea that complementary cycle partition controls robustness. The values are not implied by general anti-forcing inequalities or basic cage parameters.
